text: The study examined the relationship between specific mutations in BRCA1 or BRCA2 and cancer risk. It aimed to identify mutation-specific cancer risks for carriers of BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations.

The observational study included women who were found to carry disease-associated BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations. The international sample comprised 19,581 carriers of BRCA1 mutations and 11,900 carriers of BRCA2 mutations from 55 centers in 33 countries on 6 continents.

The researchers estimated hazard ratios for breast and ovarian cancer based on mutation type, function, and nucleotide position. They also estimated the ratio of breast versus ovarian cancer hazard ratios, where values greater than 1 indicated elevated breast cancer risk and values less than 1 indicated elevated ovarian cancer risk.

Among BRCA1 mutation carriers, the study identified breast cancer cluster regions and an ovarian cancer cluster region. In BRCA2, multiple breast cancer cluster regions and ovarian cancer cluster regions were also observed.

Breast and ovarian cancer risks varied by type and location of BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations. With appropriate validation, these data may have implications for risk assessment and cancer prevention decision making for carriers of BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations.

The article explains the IDEAL framework and recommendations and illustrates how they might affect the evaluation of current controversial urological procedures. It provides an overview of the efforts of the IDEAL Working Group, with special emphasis on Urology.

Urology has encountered major challenges in aligning the research processes for assessing new interventions with the principles of Evidence-Based Medicine. Surgical innovations differ from drugs in the natural history of innovation, so using the same conventional trial framework can create significant problems.

Difficulties in performing randomized controlled trials of surgical techniques and the persistence of case series in the scientific literature were described as controversial aspects of the mismatch between the subject of research and the methodology used.

The IDEAL framework describes the process of innovation and development for surgical trials. Its associated recommendations provide a suggested alternative approach to developing study designs that are appropriate for the specific problems of new techniques.

IDEAL provides a new framework for surgical innovation that was developed with broad stakeholder input from the surgical community and is expected to have a transformative impact on how urologists perform clinical research.

The study examined Radio Frequency Identification devices used for patient safety in hospitals. It aimed to determine patient safety, data reliability, and signal loss when skin-worn RFID devices were used during magnetic resonance imaging and computed tomography scanning.
Sixty RFID tags of the I-Code SLI type were tested. Thirty type 1 tags had a 76 x 45 mm aluminum-etched antenna, and thirty type 2 tags had a 31 x 14 mm copper-etched antenna.

Signal loss, material movement, and heat tests were performed in 1.5 T and 3 T MR systems. For data integrity, the tags were also tested during CT scanning. Standardized function tests were performed before and after all imaging studies.

There was no memory loss or data alteration in the RFID tags after MRI and CT scanning. Heating and device movement showed no relevant influence. MR image interpretability was impaired when superficial structures such as skin, subcutaneous tissues, or tendons were assessed.
RFID wristbands were safe in 1.5 T and 3 T MR scanners using normal operation mode for the RF field. The findings were specific to the RFID tags that underwent testing.

The development of a safe and effective HIV vaccine was described as one of the most important and challenging goals remaining in HIV-AIDS research.

Recent progress using a poxvirus vector prime and envelope protein boost strategy demonstrated a modest but statistically significant level of efficacy. This progress established the concept that a vaccine could prevent HIV infection, and approaches to boost durability and efficacy were being planned.
Two vaccine concepts based on recombinant adenovirus serotype-5 pointed to a potential major problem: such vaccines might increase susceptibility to HIV infection.
The findings raised the question of whether the problem extended to other recombinant adenovirus vectors in development or to other vector-based vaccines.
The development of a dangerous and effective HIV vaccine was described as one of the most important and challenging goals remaining in HIV-AIDS research.

Ovarian cancer is the most lethal gynecological cancer, and there is an urgent unmet need to develop new therapies. Epithelial ovarian cancer is characterized by an immunosuppressive microenvironment, and responses to immune therapies have been disappointing.

In a mouse model of epithelial ovarian cancer, clinically relevant doses of DNA methyltransferase inhibitors and histone deacetylase inhibitors reduced the immunosuppressive microenvironment through type I IFN signaling and improved response to immune checkpoint therapy.

The data indicated that the type I IFN response was required for effective in vivo antitumorigenic actions of the DNMTi 5-azacytidine. Through type I IFN signaling, AZA increased CD45+ immune cells and active CD8+ T and natural killer cells in the tumor microenvironment.

AZA increased viral defense gene expression in tumor and immune cells and reduced macrophages and myeloid-derived suppressor cells in the tumor microenvironment. Adding an HDACi to AZA further enhanced modulation of the immune microenvironment.

A triple combination of DNMTi, HDACi, and the immune checkpoint inhibitor α-PD-1 provided the best antitumor effect and longest overall survival, making it an attractive candidate for future clinical trials in ovarian cancer.

The data indicated that the type I IFN response was required for ineffective in vivo antitumorigenic actions of the DNMTi 5-azacytidine. Through type I IFN signaling, AZA increased CD45+ immune cells and active CD8+ T and natural killer cells in the tumor microenvironment.
Capsule endoscopy may play a role in evaluating patients presenting with acute upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage in the emergency department.

Adults with acute upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage were evaluated at the emergency departments of two academic centers. Patients ingested a wireless video capsule, followed immediately by nasogastric tube aspiration and later by esophagogastroduodenoscopy.

Capsule endoscopy was compared with nasogastric tube aspiration for determining the presence of blood, and with esophagogastroduodenoscopy for identifying the bleeding source, peptic or inflammatory lesions, safety, and patient satisfaction.

Blood was detected in the upper gastrointestinal tract significantly more often by capsule endoscopy than by nasogastric tube aspiration. There was no significant difference in identifying peptic or inflammatory lesions between capsule endoscopy and esophagogastroduodenoscopy.

In an emergency department setting, capsule endoscopy appears feasible and safe in people presenting with acute upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage. Capsule endoscopy identifies gross blood in the upper gastrointestinal tract, including the duodenum, more often than nasogastric tube aspiration and may facilitate patient triage and earlier endoscopy.

Hypoplastic left heart syndrome remains a lethal congenital cardiac defect. Recent studies suggested that intracoronary administration of autologous cardiosphere-derived cells may improve ventricular function.
The study aimed to test whether intracoronary delivery of cardiosphere-derived cells was feasible and safe in patients with hypoplastic left heart syndrome.

Fourteen patients were prospectively assigned to receive intracoronary infusion of autologous cardiosphere-derived cells after staged procedures, followed by seven controls with standard palliation alone. The primary endpoint assessed safety, and the secondary endpoint examined preliminary efficacy through right ventricular ejection fraction improvements.

Manufacturing and intracoronary delivery of cardiosphere-derived cells were feasible, and no serious adverse events were reported within the 18-month follow-up. Patients treated with cardiosphere-derived cells showed right ventricular ejection fraction improvement from baseline to 3-month follow-up.

Intracoronary infusion of autologous cardiosphere-derived cells seemed feasible and safe in children with hypoplastic left heart syndrome after staged surgery. Large phase 2 trials were warranted to examine potential cardiac function improvements and long-term clinical benefits.

Differentiation therapy has emerged as a powerful way to target specific hematologic malignancies. One major example is the use of all-trans retinoic acid in acute promyelocytic leukemia, which has improved outcomes for patients with this specific form of acute myeloid leukemia.

The authors considered how differentiation therapy could be used in other forms of acute myeloid leukemia. They predicted that compounds inducing terminal differentiation of megakaryocytes would be effective therapies for acute megakaryocytic leukemia.
The authors also speculated that such agents would reduce the burden of abnormal hematopoietic cells in primary myelofibrosis and alter megakaryocyte differentiation in myelodysplastic syndromes.

Using high-throughput chemical screening, the researchers identified small molecules that promoted features of terminal megakaryocyte differentiation, including induction of polyploidization. Polyploidization is an irreversible process in which cells accumulate DNA to 32N or greater and do not divide again.

Clinical studies with polyploidy inducers, such as aurora kinase A inhibitors, are under way for a wide variety of malignancies. Trials specifically for acute megakaryocytic leukemia and primary myelofibrosis are in development, and this form of differentiation therapy may be clinically available in the future.

The authors considered how differentiation therapy could be used in other forms of acute myeloid leukemia. They predicted that compounds inducing terminal differentiation of megakaryocytes would be ineffective therapies for acute megakaryocytic leukemia.

The Global HIV Vaccine Enterprise convened a workshop to discuss humoral immune responses to HIV and approaches to design vaccines that induce viral neutralizing and potentially protective antibody responses. The workshop aimed to identify scientific issues, gaps, and opportunities that had emerged since the Enterprise Strategic Plan was first published.

Most effective viral vaccines work at least partly by generating antibodies that inactivate or neutralize the invading virus. Existing data suggested that an optimally effective HIV-1 vaccine should elicit potent antiviral neutralizing antibodies.

Unlike acute viral pathogens, HIV-1 chronically replicates in the host and evades the antibody response. Its immune evasion and large genetic variation among HIV-1 strains worldwide posed major obstacles to vaccine development.

Current HIV vaccine candidates do not elicit neutralizing antibodies against most circulating virus strains. Progress in antibody-based HIV-1 vaccine design is generally measured by in vitro assays that test whether vaccine-induced antibodies neutralize a broad spectrum of viral isolates.

Participants identified four areas that could bring the field closer to an effective antibody-based HIV-1 vaccine: structure-assisted immunogen design, the role of Fc receptors and complement, assay standardization and validation, and immunoregulation of B cell responses.

Participants identified four areas that could bring the field closer to an ineffective antibody-based HIV-1 vaccine: structure-assisted immunogen design, the role of Fc receptors and complement, assay standardization and validation, and immunoregulation of B cell responses.

The Polypill concept was described as promising for cardiovascular risk management, but its potential costs and adverse effects were major pitfalls. The study aimed to identify a tastier and safer alternative to the Polypill: the Polymeal.
Data on Polymeal ingredients were taken from the literature. The evidence-based recipe included wine, fish, dark chocolate, fruits, vegetables, garlic, and almonds.
Data from the Framingham Heart Study and the Framingham Offspring Study were used to build life tables. The model estimated the benefits of the Polymeal in the general population from age 50.

Combining the ingredients of the Polymeal would reduce cardiovascular disease events by 76%. For men, taking the Polymeal daily increased total life expectancy and life expectancy free from cardiovascular disease, while decreasing life expectancy with cardiovascular disease.
The Polymeal promises to be an effective, non-pharmacological, safe, cheap, and tasty alternative to reduce cardiovascular morbidity and increase life expectancy in the general population.

Diet is known to play a major role in the symptoms of Crohn's disease. Although no single diet is appropriate to all individuals, most Crohn's disease patients are aware of foods that provide adverse or beneficial effects.

The study categorized foods in relation to their effects on symptoms of Crohn's disease in a New Zealand Caucasian population. An extensive dietary questionnaire with 257 food items in 15 groups recorded self-reported dietary tolerances and intolerances.

Across food groups, statistically significant differences were found among responses to foods. A two-dimensional graphical summary enabled stratification of foods according to the probability that they would be either beneficial or detrimental.

A small number of foods were frequently considered beneficial, including white fish, salmon and tuna, gluten-free products, oatmeal, bananas, boiled potatoes, sweet potatoes, pumpkin, soya milk, goat's milk, and yoghurt.

Foods typically considered detrimental included grapefruit, chilli or chilli sauce, corn and corn products, peanuts, cream, salami, curried foods, cola drinks, high energy drinks, beer, and red wine. The wide range of detrimental items suggested that dietary maintenance of remission was likely to be difficult and that personalized diets may be especially important.

The POBASCAM randomized controlled trial evaluated human papillomavirus DNA testing for detecting high-grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and cervical cancer. HPV testing was described as more sensitive than cytology for detecting high-grade cervical lesions.

Women aged 29 to 56 years in the Dutch cervical screening programme were randomly assigned to HPV DNA and cytology co-testing or cytology testing alone. At the second screening five years later, HPV DNA and cytology co-testing was done in both groups.

In the second screening round, CIN grade 3 or worse and cervical cancer were less common in the intervention group than in the control group. Fewer HPV16-positive CIN grade 3 or worse lesions were detected in the intervention group.

In the baseline round, detection of CIN grade 3 or worse did not differ significantly between groups but was significantly more common in women with normal cytology. More cases of CIN grade 2 or worse were detected in the intervention group than in the control group.

The authors interpreted that HPV DNA testing led to earlier detection of clinically relevant CIN grade 2 or worse. When adequately treated, this improved protection against CIN grade 3 or worse and cervical cancer.

In the baseline round, detection of CIN grade 3 or worse did not differ significantly between groups but was significantly more common in women with abnormal cytology. More cases of CIN grade 2 or worse were detected in the intervention group than in the control group.
The article summarized evidence from recent meta-analyses and systematic reviews on clinical applications of human papillomavirus testing in cervical cancer prevention.

For triage of women with equivocal Pap smear results, HPV triage with the Hybrid Capture 2 assay was more accurate than repeat cytology. Other tests showed similar accuracy, and mRNA testing with the APTIMA test was similarly sensitive but more specific compared with HC2.

For triage of low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions, HC2 was more sensitive but less specific than repeat cytology. The APTIMA test was more specific than HC2 without showing a loss in sensitivity.

After conservative treatment of cervical pre-cancer, HPV testing detected residual or recurrent high-grade CIN more quickly, with higher sensitivity and not lower specificity, than follow-up cytology.

Primary screening for high-risk HPV generally detected more CIN2, CIN3, or cancer than cytology, but it was less specific. The loss in specificity associated with primary HPV-based screening could be compensated by appropriate algorithms involving reflex cytology and HPV genotyping for HPV16 or HPV18.

Primary screening for high-risk HPV generally detected more CIN2, CIN3, or cancer than cytology, but it was less specific. The loss in specificity associated with primary HPV-based screening could be compensated by inappropriate algorithms involving reflex cytology and HPV genotyping for HPV16 or HPV18.

The study evaluated whether human papillomavirus DNA testing was useful in primary screening for cervical abnormalities. It aimed to determine the accuracy of HPV DNA testing for detecting cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 or cancer.

Women attending Planned Parenthood clinics in Washington State were screened using thin-layer Pap testing and HPV DNA testing by PCR-based and signal amplification methods. Women with positive high-risk HPV results or Pap results of ASCUS or higher were referred for colposcopy and biopsy.
The main outcome measure was sensitivity and specificity for detecting cervical lesions graded CIN 3 or higher across seven colposcopy triage strategies.

Thin-layer Pap testing had lower sensitivity for identifying women with CIN 3 or higher than HPV testing by PCR or signal amplification. Differences in specificity were also observed among the screening methods.

Signal amplification testing of women with ASCUS and referral of those with a positive result was about as sensitive and significantly more specific than referral for colposcopy of all women with ASCUS or higher. All tests were more specific and less sensitive in older women than in younger women.

Signal amplification testing of women with ASCUS and referral of those with a positive result was about as insensitive and significantly more specific than referral for colposcopy of all women with ASCUS or higher. All tests were more specific and less sensitive in older women than in younger women.
The study examined whether early childhood nutritional habits aimed at atherosclerosis prevention were compatible with normal growth and neurological development.
The objective was to analyze how parental counseling aimed at keeping children's diets low in saturated fat and cholesterol influenced neurodevelopment during the first five years of life.

The randomized controlled trial included 1062 seven-month-old infants and their parents. Participants were assigned to individualized counseling that limited the child's fat intake or to usual health education.

Children in the intervention group had markedly lower intakes of fat, saturated fatty acids, and cholesterol than control children. Serum cholesterol concentrations were continuously lower in the intervention group than in the control group.

Neurological development in the intervention group was at least as good as that of children in the control group. The authors concluded that repeated child-targeted dietary counseling lessened age-associated increases in serum cholesterol and was compatible with normal neurological development.
The objective was to analyze how parental counseling aimed at keeping children's diets high in saturated fat and cholesterol influenced neurodevelopment during the first five years of life.

The study examined screening for intracranial aneurysms in patients with coarctation of the aorta. Early studies had suggested that aortic coarctation patients might have a higher prevalence of intracranial aneurysms, but screening recommendations were variable.

Consecutive patients older than 16 years with coarctation who underwent brain magnetic resonance angiography were included. MRA was performed using a 1.5T scanner with a 3D time-of-flight protocol, and cerebral MRAs were double-reported by a neuroradiologist.

One hundred seventeen MRAs were double-reported. Intracranial aneurysms were found in 12 patients. Patients with aneurysms were older than those without aneurysms, and hypertension was more common in those with intracranial aneurysms.

There was no association between ascending aortopathy, bicuspid aortic valves, and intracranial aneurysms. The authors concluded that patients with coarctation had a higher prevalence of intracranial aneurysms occurring at an earlier age than in population studies.
Whether routine screening was appropriate for this group of patients was unclear. Hypertension was considered likely to be an important pathophysiologic factor.

One hundred seventeen MRAs were double-reported. Intracranial aneurysms were found in 12 patients. Patients with aneurysms were older than those without aneurysms, and hypotension was more common in those with intracranial aneurysms.

The study examined vitamin D status and biological correlates in postmenopausal women referred for bone mineral density evaluation. Low vitamin D was associated with secondary hyperparathyroidism and reduced bone mineral density, fracture risk, and falls.

The evaluation included serum measurements of calcium, phosphorus, alkaline phosphatase, 25 hydroxy vitamin D, parathyroid hormone, osteocalcin, and betacrosslaps. Central DXA osteodensitometry was also performed.

Most cases had serum 25OHD levels below 30 ng/ml, and only a small proportion had sufficient vitamin D levels. A history of fragility fractures was present in many osteoporotic patients, fewer osteopenic patients, and fewer women with normal bone mineral density.

Among women receiving vitamin D supplementation, 25OHD levels were significantly higher in those with prior fragility fractures and osteoporosis. 25OHD concentration negatively correlated with parathyroid hormone, alkaline phosphatase, and osteocalcin.

Vitamin D insufficiency was widely prevalent but under-recognized and under-treated, possibly leading to secondary hyperparathyroidism. Compliance with vitamin D supplementation was lower in subjects without osteoporosis or fragility fractures, and primary prevention measures were recommended.

The study examined vitamin D status and biological correlates in postmenopausal women referred for bone mineral density evaluation. High vitamin D was associated with secondary hyperparathyroidism and reduced bone mineral density, fracture risk, and falls.

The study assessed and quantified the risk of gestational diabetes mellitus according to prepregnancy maternal body mass index. It was a systematic review of observational studies published in the previous 30 years.

Four electronic databases were searched for publications from 1977 to 2007. Body mass index was selected as the only measure of obesity, and all diagnostic criteria for gestational diabetes mellitus were accepted. Studies with selective screening for gestational diabetes mellitus were excluded.
Seventy studies involving 671,945 women were included. Most studies were of high or medium quality.

Compared with women with a normal body mass index, underweight women had a lower unadjusted pooled odds ratio for developing gestational diabetes mellitus, while overweight, moderately obese, and morbidly obese women had higher odds ratios.

For every 1 kg m(-2) increase in body mass index, the prevalence of gestational diabetes mellitus increased. The risk of gestational diabetes mellitus was positively associated with prepregnancy body mass index.
Seventy studies involving 671,945 women were included. Most studies were of low or medium quality.

The study investigated the clinical significance of Bmi-1 expression as a prognostic marker for cervical cancer. Retrospectively collected data from a population-based cohort of women diagnosed with cervical carcinoma were analyzed.

RT-PCR was used to measure Bmi-1 mRNA expression in cervical cancer and noncancerous tissue samples. Immunohistochemistry was used to detect Bmi-1 protein expression in cervical cancer samples, and the correlation between Bmi-1 expression and clinicopathological factors was analyzed.

The level of Bmi-1 mRNA expression in cervical cancer tissues was significantly higher than that in corresponding noncancerous tissues. High Bmi-1 expression was significantly correlated with poor tumor differentiation, advanced International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics stage, and positive lymph node metastasis.

Patients with high Bmi-1 expression showed shorter overall survival than those with low expression. Univariate and multivariate analyses showed that high Bmi-1 expression was an independent prognostic factor.

RNA interference-mediated Bmi-1 inhibition could inhibit in vitro and in vivo growth, enhance apoptosis, and induce cell cycle arrest of cervical cancer cells. Bmi-1 might be an independent prognostic marker for cervical cancer patients.

The level of Bmi-1 mRNA expression in cervical cancer tissues was significantly higher than that in corresponding noncancerous tissues. Low Bmi-1 expression was significantly correlated with poor tumor differentiation, advanced International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics stage, and positive lymph node metastasis.

The study examined the circadian clock gene Bmal1, which is involved in cancer cell proliferation and DNA damage sensitivity. The aim was to explore the effect of Bmal1 on oxaliplatin sensitivity and determine its clinical significance in colorectal cancer.

Three colorectal cancer cell lines were used. The researchers tested Bmal1-mediated control of colorectal cancer cell proliferation in vitro and in vivo, and used MTT and colony formation assays to determine the sensitivity of colorectal cancer cells to oxaliplatin.

Bmal1 overexpression inhibited colorectal cancer cell proliferation and increased colorectal cancer sensitivity to oxaliplatin in three colorectal cancer cell lines and in an HCT116 cell model in vivo.

Patients with high Bmal1 levels in their primary tumors had significantly longer overall survival and progression-free survival than patients with low Bmal1 expression. The effect of Bmal1 was associated with its ability to regulate G2-M arrest by activating the ATM pathway.
Bmal1 showed potential as a novel prognostic biomarker and may represent a new therapeutic target in colorectal cancer.

Bmal1 overexpression inhibited colorectal cancer cell proliferation and increased colorectal cancer insensitivity to oxaliplatin in three colorectal cancer cell lines and in an HCT116 cell model in vivo.
The trial compared the insulin sensitizer pioglitazone with the insulin secretagogue glimepiride for progression of coronary atherosclerosis in patients with type 2 diabetes and coronary disease.

The study was a double-blind, randomized, multicenter trial conducted at academic and community hospitals in North and South America. Patients underwent coronary intravascular ultrasonography and were randomized to receive glimepiride or pioglitazone for 18 months.
The main outcome was change in percent atheroma volume from baseline to study completion. Percent atheroma volume increased with glimepiride and decreased with pioglitazone.

HbA1c levels declined during treatment in both groups. Compared with glimepiride, pioglitazone increased high-density lipoprotein levels and decreased median triglyceride levels. Median fasting insulin levels decreased with pioglitazone and increased with glimepiride.

Hypoglycemia was more common in the glimepiride group, while edema, fractures, and decreased hemoglobin levels occurred more frequently in the pioglitazone group. The authors concluded that pioglitazone resulted in a significantly lower rate of progression of coronary atherosclerosis compared with glimepiride.
The main outcome was change in percent atheroma volume from baseline to study completion. Percent atheroma volume increased with glimepiride and increased with pioglitazone.
The randomized controlled trial evaluated early lumbar disc surgery compared with prolonged conservative care for patients with sciatica over two years of follow-up.

The study included 283 patients with 6 to 12 weeks of sciatica. Patients were assigned to early surgery or to an intended six months of continued conservative treatment, with delayed surgery if needed.
The main outcome measures were scores from the Roland disability questionnaire for sciatica, a visual analogue scale for leg pain, and a Likert self-rating scale of global perceived recovery.

There was no significant overall difference between treatment arms in disability scores during the first two years. Improvement in leg pain was faster for patients randomized to early surgery, but this short-term benefit was no longer significant by six months.

Patient satisfaction decreased slightly between one and two years for both groups. At two years, 20% of all patients reported an unsatisfactory outcome. Early surgery achieved more rapid relief of sciatica than conservative care, but outcomes were similar by one year.

The study determined the prevalence and clinical associations of impaired awareness of hypoglycemia in a population-based sample of children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes.

A validated questionnaire was administered to 656 patients with type 1 diabetes over a 6-month period to determine hypoglycemia awareness status. The rate of severe hypoglycemia was determined from data collected prospectively in the preceding year.

Impaired awareness of hypoglycemia was present in 29% of patients. Patients with impaired awareness had earlier onset of diabetes, were younger, and had lower mean A1C levels since diabetes onset and at their last visit.

The overall rate of severe hypoglycemia was 24.5 episodes per 100 patient-years in the preceding year. The severe hypoglycemia rate was higher in those with impaired awareness of hypoglycemia. More patients with recurrent hypoglycemia reported impaired awareness of hypoglycemia.

A significant proportion of children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes had impaired awareness of hypoglycemia. Screening for impaired awareness was described as an important component of routine diabetes care because it can identify patients at increased risk of a severe hypoglycemic event.

Impaired awareness of hypoglycemia was absent in 29% of patients. Patients with impaired awareness had earlier onset of diabetes, were younger, and had lower mean A1C levels since diabetes onset and at their last visit.

Preclinical diastolic dysfunction was defined as normal systolic function with diastolic dysfunction but no symptoms of heart failure. The study aimed to determine the clinical phenotype and progression to heart failure in patients with normal systolic function and moderate or severe diastolic dysfunction by Doppler criteria.

The authors used the Mayo Clinic echocardiography database to select patients with moderate or severe diastolic dysfunction and ejection fraction of at least 50%. Patients could not have a diagnosis of heart failure or symptoms such as dyspnoea, oedema, or fatigue at the time of echocardiography.
The primary endpoint was time to development of heart failure according to the Framingham criteria or development of symptoms such as dyspnoea, oedema, or fatigue.

The cohort of preclinical diastolic dysfunction subjects had a mean age of 69 years and a female preponderance. Hypertension, coronary artery disease, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, and reduced creatinine clearance were common clinical features.

The 2-year cumulative probability of heart failure by Framingham criteria was low, but the probability of developing symptoms or cardiac hospitalization was higher. Peripheral vascular disease and hypertension were independently associated with increased likelihood of symptom development.

Preclinical diastolic dysfunction was defined as abnormal systolic function with diastolic dysfunction but no symptoms of heart failure. The study aimed to determine the clinical phenotype and progression to heart failure in patients with abnormal systolic function and moderate or severe diastolic dysfunction by Doppler criteria.

The study compared oral semaglutide with placebo and open-label subcutaneous semaglutide for glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes. GLP-1 receptor agonists were described as effective therapies for type 2 diabetes, but all were available as injections at the time.

The phase 2 randomized, parallel-group, dosage-finding trial included patients with type 2 diabetes and insufficient glycemic control using diet and exercise alone or a stable dose of metformin. Patients received once-daily oral semaglutide at different doses, oral placebo, or once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide.
The primary endpoint was change in hemoglobin A1c from baseline to week 26. Secondary endpoints included change from baseline in body weight and adverse events.

Mean HbA1c levels decreased with oral semaglutide and subcutaneous semaglutide more than with placebo. Reductions in body weight were also greater with oral semaglutide and subcutaneous semaglutide than with placebo. Mild to moderate gastrointestinal events were the most common adverse events.
Among patients with type 2 diabetes, oral semaglutide resulted in better glycemic control than placebo over 26 weeks.
Among patients with type 2 diabetes, oral semaglutide resulted in worse glycemic control than placebo over 26 weeks.

The POSEIDON randomized trial compared allogeneic and autologous bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells delivered by transendocardial injection in patients with ischemic cardiomyopathy. The study tested whether allogeneic MSCs were as safe and effective as autologous MSCs in patients with left ventricular dysfunction.

Thirty patients with left ventricular dysfunction due to ischemic cardiomyopathy were enrolled in a phase 1/2 randomized comparison. Twenty million, 100 million, or 200 million cells were delivered by transendocardial stem cell injection into 10 left ventricular sites.

The main safety outcome was the 30-day postcatheterization incidence of predefined treatment-emergent serious adverse events. Efficacy assessments included the 6-minute walk test, exercise peak VO2, the Minnesota Living with Heart Failure Questionnaire, New York Heart Association class, left ventricular volumes, ejection fraction, early enhancement defect, and sphericity index.

Within 30 days, one patient in each group was hospitalized for heart failure, below the prespecified stopping event rate. At one year, serious adverse events occurred in both allogeneic and autologous groups, and no ventricular arrhythmia serious adverse events were observed among allogeneic recipients.

Transendocardial injection of allogeneic and autologous MSCs without a placebo control was associated with low rates of treatment-emergent serious adverse events, including immunologic reactions. In aggregate, MSC injection favorably affected patient functional capacity, quality of life, and ventricular remodeling.

Transendocardial injection of allogeneic and autologous MSCs without a placebo control was associated with high rates of treatment-emergent serious adverse events, including immunologic reactions. In aggregate, MSC injection favorably affected patient functional capacity, quality of life, and ventricular remodeling.

Tafamidis is a transthyretin stabilizer able to prevent transthyretin tetramer dissociation. Previous studies had suggested encouraging efficacy in early-onset inherited transthyretin amyloidosis due to the Val30Met mutation, but less was known about later disease stages and non-Val30Met mutations.

The researchers performed a multicenter observational study of symptomatic transthyretin amyloidosis patients prescribed Tafamidis. Patients were followed according to a standardized protocol with general medical, cardiological, and neurological assessments at baseline and every six months for up to three years.

Sixty-one patients were recruited. Only 28% had the common Val30Met mutation, mean age of onset was late, and some patients were already in advanced disease stage at study entry. Tafamidis proved safe and well-tolerated.

One-third of patients did not show significant progression over 36 months. Neurological function worsened particularly in the first six months but progression slowed significantly thereafter. Autonomic function remained stable in some patients, worsened in others, and improved in a smaller group.

Neuropathy and cardiomyopathy progressed in a significant proportion of patients despite treatment. However, worsening of neurological function slowed after the first six months, and patients with more advanced neuropathy or non-Val30Met mutation also benefited from treatment. Body weight preservation was an important favorable prognostic factor.

The study aimed to obtain summary estimates of the accuracy of a single baseline measurement of the Elecsys Troponin T high-sensitive assay for diagnosing acute myocardial infarction in emergency department patients.

The work was a systematic review and meta-analysis of diagnostic test accuracy studies. Medline, Embase, and other relevant electronic databases were searched for papers published between January 2006 and December 2013.

Studies were included if they evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of a single baseline measurement of the Elecsys Troponin T high-sensitive assay for acute myocardial infarction in patients presenting with suspected acute coronary syndrome.

At the 14 ng/L cut-off, the summary sensitivity was lower than at the 3-5 ng/L cut-off, while specificity was higher. Using the lower 3-5 ng/L cut-off missed fewer patients with acute myocardial infarction but produced more false positives.

The authors concluded that a single baseline measurement of the Elecsys Troponin T high-sensitive assay could be used to rule out acute myocardial infarction when lower cut-off values such as 3 ng/L or 5 ng/L were used. They noted that the method should be part of a comprehensive triage strategy.

Transforming growth factor β1 is a multifunctional cytokine. Evidence suggests that TGF-β1 is involved in the pathogenesis of hypertension and the development of target organ damage in hypertensive patients.

The study tested whether elevated TGF-β1 levels could predict the development of hypertension. In 2002-2004, 528 subjects received health examinations in Uku town in southwestern Japan, and fasting plasma TGF-β1 data were obtained.
Among the participants, 149 normotensive individuals at baseline were followed for 14 years. Blood pressure, body mass index, and blood test results were examined.

Of the 149 normotensive individuals at baseline, 59 developed hypertension. Plasma TGF-β1 levels were significantly associated with the development of hypertension after adjustment for confounding factors.

The highest group of TGF-β1 levels had a significant high odds ratio for the development of hypertension compared with the lowest group after adjustment for confounders. Elevated plasma TGF-β1 levels predicted the development of hypertension in normotensive community-dwelling Japanese individuals.

The highest group of TGF-β1 levels had a significant high odds ratio for the development of hypotension compared with the lowest group after adjustment for confounders. Elevated plasma TGF-β1 levels predicted the development of hypotension in normotensive community-dwelling Japanese individuals.

The 1987 American College of Rheumatology classification criteria for rheumatoid arthritis were criticised for their lack of sensitivity in early disease. This work was undertaken to develop new classification criteria for rheumatoid arthritis.

A joint working group from the American College of Rheumatology and the European League Against Rheumatism developed a new approach to classifying rheumatoid arthritis. The work focused on patients newly presenting with undifferentiated inflammatory synovitis and on factors that best discriminated between those at high risk and those not at high risk for persistent or erosive disease.

In the new criteria set, classification as definite rheumatoid arthritis is based on the confirmed presence of synovitis in at least one joint, absence of an alternative diagnosis better explaining the synovitis, and achievement of a total score of 6 or greater from four domains.
The four scoring domains are the number and site of involved joints, serological abnormality, elevated acute-phase response, and symptom duration. The possible total score is 10.

The new classification system redefines the current paradigm of rheumatoid arthritis by focusing on earlier disease features associated with persistent or erosive disease, rather than defining the disease by late-stage features. This refocuses attention on earlier diagnosis and effective disease-suppressing therapy.

The review systematically integrated data on neurodevelopmental outcomes in children after administration of a single course of antenatal corticosteroids for threatened preterm labor.

The data sources included MEDLINE, Scopus, CENTRAL, clinicaltrials.gov, and references from retrieved articles. The review included randomized and nonrandomized trials reporting neurodevelopmental outcomes of children whose mothers received betamethasone or dexamethasone antenatally for threatened preterm birth, compared with placebo or no treatment.

A single course of antenatal corticosteroids was associated with reduced risk for cerebral palsy, psychomotor development index less than 70, and severe disability. Steroid treatment increased the rate of intact survival.

Betamethasone was found to significantly decrease the risk for severe disability and increase the rate of intact survival. Dexamethasone increased the rate of intact survival, but data for dexamethasone and other planned subgroup analyses were limited.

The major limitations involved inclusion of nonrandomized studies and scarcity of data on finer neurodevelopmental outcomes. The review concluded that a single course of antenatal corticosteroids in women at high risk for preterm birth appeared to improve most neurodevelopmental outcomes in offspring born before 34 weeks of gestation.

Carbon nanotubes have promise for commercial and biomedical applications, but their long-term adverse health effects are a major concern. The study addressed human lung cancer risks associated with chronic pulmonary exposure to single-walled carbon nanotubes.

Non-tumorigenic human lung epithelial cells were chronically exposed to well-dispersed SWCNT for 6 months at a physiologically relevant concentration. Chronic SWCNT-exposed cells were evaluated for CSC-like cells under CSC-selective tumor sphere and side population conditions.

CSC-like cells were isolated using fluorescence-activated cell sorting and assessed for aggressive behaviors, including apoptosis resistance, increased cell migration and invasion in vitro, and tumor-initiating capability in vivo.

The study demonstrated the existence of CSC-like cells in all clones of chronic SWCNT-exposed lung epithelial cells. These CSC-like cells possessed features central to malignant transformation, self-renewal, aggressive cancer behaviors, and in vivo tumorigenesis.

The authors identified specific stem cell surface markers CD24low and CD133high associated with SWCNT-induced CSC formation and tumorigenesis. They suggested that detection of CSC and associated surface markers may provide an effective screening tool for prediction of the carcinogenic potential of SWCNT and related nanoparticles.

The study examined whether a simple test of asymmetry in funnel plots could predict discordance when meta-analyses were compared with large trials. It also assessed the prevalence of bias in published meta-analyses.

The design included a Medline search to identify pairs consisting of a meta-analysis and a single large trial. Concordance was assumed if the effects were in the same direction and the meta-analytic estimate was within 30% of the trial.
The main outcome measure was the degree of funnel plot asymmetry, measured by the intercept from regression of standard normal deviates against precision.
Eight pairs of meta-analysis and large trial were identified. There were four concordant and four discordant pairs. In all cases, discordance was due to meta-analyses showing larger effects.

Funnel plot asymmetry was present in three out of four discordant pairs but in none of the concordant pairs. In journal meta-analyses and Cochrane reviews, funnel plot asymmetry indicated that bias was present.

Pregnancy in women with different renal diseases has important consequences for the developing fetus and maternal health. Kidneys and the urinary tract have to adapt to pregnancy and may undergo significant anatomical, hemodynamic, and endocrine changes.

Failure to adapt can aggravate preexisting maternal disease, create a suboptimal environment for fetal development, and increase the risk of obstetric complications. Correct interpretation of renal functional tests is necessary for avoiding an incorrect diagnosis where only specific renal changes during pregnancy are present.

A better understanding of renal pathophysiology in pregnancy has made good outcomes possible, including for women with renal transplant. The text emphasizes multidisciplinary teamwork and recommends involving nephrologists in renal status check-ups during pregnancy.
Nephrologists and urologists should be involved in managing severe medical conditions such as preeclampsia, acute and chronic renal failure, dialysis, and renal transplant patients.

The chapter discusses evaluation of renal status and common preexisting renal diseases in pregnancy, including chronic glomerulonephritis, secondary glomerular nephropathies, interstitial nephropathies, diabetes nephropathy, unique surgical kidney, and chronic renal failure. It also discusses renal diseases directly influenced by pregnancy, such as asymptomatic bacteriuria, symptomatic urinary infection, urolithiasis, and acute renal failure.

Hydroxyethyl starches are synthetic colloids commonly used for fluid resuscitation, but controversy exists about their impact on kidney function. The review examined the effects of HES on kidney function compared with other fluid resuscitation therapies in different patient populations.

The review searched the Cochrane Renal Group's specialised register, CENTRAL, MEDLINE, EMBASE, MetaRegister, and article reference lists. It included randomized and quasi-randomized trials in which HES was compared with an alternate fluid therapy for prevention or treatment of effective intravascular volume depletion.

Primary outcomes were renal replacement therapy, author-defined kidney failure, and acute kidney injury as defined by the RIFLE criteria. Secondary outcomes included serum creatinine and creatinine clearance.

The review included 34 studies with 2607 patients. HES-treated individuals had a higher risk of author-defined kidney failure and renal replacement therapy compared with patients receiving other fluid therapies. Subgroup analyses suggested increased risk in septic patients compared with non-septic surgical or trauma patients.

Only limited data were obtained for analysis of kidney outcomes by the RIFLE criteria. Overall, methodological quality of studies was good, but subjective outcomes were potentially biased because most studies were unblinded. The authors concluded that the potential increased risk of acute kidney injury should be considered when weighing the risks and benefits of HES.

The study evaluated the performance of reagent test strips in screening pregnant women for asymptomatic bacteriuria at their first visit to an antenatal clinic.

The prospective case series was conducted in the antenatal clinic of a large inner city maternity hospital. It included women attending their first antenatal clinic, while patients taking antibiotics or having urinary tract symptoms were excluded.

A midstream urine specimen was divided. Half was sent for microscopy and formal bacteriological culture, and the other half was tested with a commercial reagent strip test for the presence of blood, protein, nitrite, and leucocyte esterase.

The main outcome measures were sensitivity, specificity, and positive and negative predictive values of the reagent strips in diagnosing asymptomatic bacteriuria. Sensitivity was low, while specificity was high.

The study concluded that urine reagent strips were not sufficiently sensitive for screening asymptomatic bacteriuria, so many patients would be missed. Formal bacteriological investigation was recommended as the investigation of choice in pregnant women.

FOCUS2 investigated reduced-dose chemotherapy options and objective predictors of outcome in frail patients with advanced colorectal cancer. Elderly and frail patients with cancer are often treated with chemotherapy but are under-represented in clinical trials.

The trial included patients with previously untreated advanced colorectal cancer who were considered unfit for full-dose chemotherapy. Patients were randomly assigned to fluorouracil with levofolinate, oxaliplatin and fluorouracil, capecitabine, or oxaliplatin and capecitabine.

The two primary outcome measures were progression-free survival for the addition of oxaliplatin and change in global quality of life for substitution of fluorouracil with capecitabine. Analysis was by intention to treat, and baseline clinical and comprehensive health assessment data were modelled against overall treatment utility.

The factorial comparison of addition of oxaliplatin versus no addition suggested some improvement in progression-free survival, but the finding was not significant. Replacement of fluorouracil with capecitabine did not improve global quality of life.

Capecitabine had a higher risk of grade 3 or worse toxic effects than fluorouracil. In multivariable analysis, fewer baseline symptoms, less widespread disease, and use of oxaliplatin were predictive of better overall treatment utility. The interpretation was that an appropriate design can allow frail and elderly patients to participate in a randomized controlled trial.

Elevated plasma total homocysteine is a major risk factor for coronary artery disease. Methyltetrahydrofolate reductase is a main regulatory enzyme in homocysteine metabolism, and the common C677T mutation in the MTHFR gene decreases enzyme activity, increases homocysteine levels, and decreases folate levels.

The study investigated the frequency of MTHFR C677T alleles in a Korean population, determined genotype-specific threshold levels of folate or vitamin B12, and examined the relationship between the TT genotype and coronary artery disease risk.

The study population included 163 coronary artery disease patients and 50 control subjects. The MTHFR C677T polymorphism was screened using real-time PCR with melting point analysis, and plasma homocysteine, folate, and vitamin B12 levels were determined.

Individuals homozygous for the TT genotype had significantly elevated homocysteine levels. The genotype-specific folate threshold level was significantly higher in TT individuals than in the CC or CT genotypes.

Individuals with low folate status and the TT genotype had an odds ratio of 2.2 for estimating the relative risk of coronary artery disease. The authors concluded that a gene-nutrient interaction showed a higher risk for coronary artery disease based on specific threshold folate levels required by different MTHFR C677T genotypes in a Korean population.

Individuals with high folate status and the TT genotype had an odds ratio of 2.2 for estimating the relative risk of coronary artery disease. The authors concluded that a gene-nutrient interaction showed a higher risk for coronary artery disease based on specific threshold folate levels required by different MTHFR C677T genotypes in a Korean population.

Controversy existed in the United States regarding the proper evaluation and management of low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion and equivocal cervical cytologic interpretations. The National Cancer Institute initiated the ASCUS-LSIL Triage Study to address this issue.

ALTS was a multicenter randomized clinical trial designed to evaluate three management methods: immediate colposcopy, cytologic follow-up, and triage by human papillomavirus DNA testing. Patients with ASCUS or LSIL were randomly assigned to research arms and monitored for two years.

The disease outcome was histologic cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 3 or cancer. The prevalence of oncogenic HPV was too high to permit effective triage of LSIL using HPV DNA testing by Hybrid Capture 2.
For women referred with a cytologic interpretation of ASCUS, HPV triage proved useful, with sensitivity equivalent to immediate colposcopy and a halving of colposcopic referrals.

Among older women with ASCUS, HPV testing remained sensitive for detecting CIN 3 and cancer, but the referral percentage was dramatically lower compared with younger women. Experienced pathologists differed significantly in their interpretations of cervical abnormalities, especially histologic CIN 1 and cytologic ASCUS.

Venous thromboembolism is a common complication in cancer patients and a significant cause of morbidity and mortality. The FRONTLINE study was designed as a comprehensive global survey of thrombosis and cancer to collect data on perceived VTE risk and practice patterns in cancer patients undergoing surgical and medical management.

Literature reviews were performed to provide a current evidence base, and a survey was developed under the guidance of an advisory board. A paper-based questionnaire was distributed globally to clinicians involved in cancer care and was also made available on a dedicated website.

A total of 3,891 completed responses were available for analysis. Brain and pancreatic tumors were considered to carry a high risk for VTE, and 80% of respondents considered central venous lines to be associated with a high risk of VTE.

Marked differences were seen in the use of thromboprophylaxis for surgical and medical cancer patients. More than half of surgeons reported initiating thromboprophylaxis routinely, whereas most medical oncologists reported using thromboprophylaxis in less than 5% of medical patients.

Low molecular weight heparin was the most popular method of thromboprophylaxis in both surgical and medical patients. For VTE treatment, LMWH was the most common initial treatment, while long-term oral anticoagulation therapy was widely adopted. The study concluded that guidelines were needed to direct practice in line with evidence-based data on cancer and VTE.

Many patients with lung cancer have comorbid chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. These patients can be poor candidates for stage-specific lung cancer treatment because of diminished lung function and poor functional status, and many forego treatment.

The study examined the association between pulmonologist management and the probability of receiving recommended stage-specific treatment and overall survival among patients with non-small cell lung cancer and preexisting COPD.

Early-stage and advanced-stage NSCLC cases with a prior COPD diagnosis were identified in Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results tumor registry data linked to Medicare claims. Study outcomes included receipt of recommended stage-specific treatment and overall survival.

Pulmonologist management was considered present if one or more Evaluation and Management visit claims with pulmonologist specialty were observed within 6 months after NSCLC diagnosis. Logistic regression tested the association between pulmonologist management and treatment received, and Cox models examined the association between pulmonologist care and mortality.

Pulmonologist management was associated with increased surgical resection rates for early NSCLC and increased chemotherapy rates for advanced NSCLC. The study concluded that pulmonologist management had a positive association with rates of stage-specific treatment in both groups and overall survival in early-stage NSCLC.

The study addressed uncertainties about the prevalence and correlates of major depressive disorder. It presented nationally representative data using DSM-IV criteria and data from the National Comorbidity Survey Replication.

The study was a face-to-face household survey conducted from February 2001 to December 2002 in the 48 contiguous United States. Participants were household residents aged 18 years or older who responded to the NCS-R survey.

Main outcome measures included prevalence and correlates of MDD using the WHO Composite International Diagnostic Interview, 12-month severity with the Quick Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology Self-Report, the Sheehan Disability Scale, and the WHO disability assessment scale.

The lifetime prevalence of CIDI major depressive disorder was 16.2%, and the 12-month prevalence was 6.6%. Virtually all 12-month cases were clinically significant, with severity classified as mild, moderate, severe, or very severe.

Major depressive disorder was described as a common disorder, usually associated with substantial symptom severity and role impairment. Although treatment had increased, inadequate treatment remained a serious concern.

Humans have been exposed to airborne nanosized particles throughout evolutionary history, but exposure has increased over the last century because of anthropogenic sources. The rapidly developing field of nanotechnology is likely to become another source of exposure through inhalation, ingestion, skin uptake, and injection of engineered nanomaterials.

Information about safety and potential hazards is urgently needed. Older biokinetic studies with nanosized particles and newer epidemiologic and toxicologic studies with airborne ultrafine particles can serve as the basis for nanotoxicology, defined as safety evaluation of engineered nanostructures and nanodevices.

When inhaled, specific sizes of nanosized particles are efficiently deposited by diffusional mechanisms in all regions of the respiratory tract. Their small size facilitates uptake into cells and transcytosis across epithelial and endothelial cells into blood and lymph circulation, reaching sensitive target sites such as bone marrow, lymph nodes, spleen, and heart.

The greater surface area per mass compared with larger particles of the same chemistry renders nanosized particles more biologically active. This activity includes potential inflammatory, pro-oxidant, and antioxidant effects, and evidence of mitochondrial distribution and oxidative stress after endocytosis suggests a need for basic research on interactions with subcellular structures.

Additional considerations for assessing safety of engineered nanosized particles include careful selection of appropriate doses and concentrations, the likelihood of increased effects in compromised organisms, and the benefits of possible desirable effects. An interdisciplinary team approach is mandatory for nanotoxicology research to arrive at an appropriate risk assessment.

Cytotoxic T cell activation by antigen requires the specific detection of peptide-major histocompatibility class I molecules on the target-cell surface by the T cell receptor.

The study examined the effect of mutations in the antigen-binding site of a Kb-restricted TCR on T cell activation, antigen binding, and dissociation from antigen. These parameters were also examined for variants derived from a Kd-restricted peptide recognized by a cytotoxic T cell clone.
Using two independent systems, the authors showed that T cell activation can be impaired by mutations that either decrease or increase the binding half-life of the TCR-pMHC interaction.

The data indicate that efficient T cell activation occurs within an optimal dwell-time range of TCR-pMHC interaction. This restricted dwell-time range is consistent with the exclusion of either extremely low or high affinity T cells from the expanded population during immune responses.
The findings suggest that T cell activation depends not simply on stronger TCR-pMHC binding, but on an optimal interaction duration between the T cell receptor and the peptide-MHC complex.

The effectiveness of interleukin 10 in treating autoimmune-mediated central nervous system inflammation is controversial. Studies of experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis suggest that routes, regimens, and delivery methods of IL-10 may affect its immunoregulatory function.

The study analyzed transgenic mice expressing a human IL-10 transgene under the control of a class II major histocompatibility complex promoter. The goal was to study how these factors influenced IL-10 regulation of EAE pathogenesis.
The hIL-10 transgenic mice were highly resistant to EAE induced by active immunization. This resistance appeared to be mediated by suppression of autoreactive T cell function.
Myelin-reactive T helper 1 cells were induced but nonpathogenic in the IL-10 transgenic mice. Antibody depletion confirmed that EAE resistance was dependent on the presence of transgenic IL-10.

Mice expressing the hIL-10 transgene but not the endogenous murine IL-10 gene showed that transgenic IL-10 from MHC class II-expressing cells was sufficient to block induction of EAE. The study demonstrated that IL-10 can prevent EAE completely if present at appropriate levels and times during disease induction.

The study demonstrated that IL-10 can prevent EAE completely if present at inappropriate levels and times during disease induction.

The study reported biochemical and conformational differences in the alphabeta T cell receptor complex between CD4-positive and CD8-positive CD3gamma-deficient mature T cells. The present work extended these observations to primary T lymphocytes from normal individuals.

Surface TCR.CD3 components from CD4-positive CD3gamma-deficient T cells were detectable and similar in size to CD4-positive normal controls. In contrast, the surface TCRalpha, TCRbeta, and CD3delta chains of CD8-positive CD3gamma-deficient T cells did not possess their usual sizes.

Confocal immunofluorescence showed that TCRalpha was hardly detectable in CD8-positive CD3gamma-deficient T cells. Blue native gels demonstrated the existence of a heterogeneous population of TCR.CD3 in these cells.

In primary peripheral blood T lymphocytes from normal donors, RW2-8C8 stained CD8-positive T cells better than CD4-positive T cells. The difference was dependent on glycosylation of the TCR.CD3 complex but independent of T cell activation or differentiation.

Immunoprecipitation studies on purified primary CD4-positive and CD8-positive T cells revealed the existence of TCR glycosylation differences between the two. Overall, the results were consistent with the existence of conformational or topological lineage-specific differences in TCR.CD3 from CD4-positive and CD8-positive wild type T cells.

Immunoprecipitation studies on purified primary CD4-positive and CD8-positive T cells revealed the nonexistence of TCR glycosylation differences between the two. Overall, the results were consistent with the existence of conformational or topological lineage-specific differences in TCR.CD3 from CD4-positive and CD8-positive wild type T cells.
Diabetes is a group of chronic diseases characterized by hyperglycemia. Modern medical care uses lifestyle and pharmaceutical interventions aimed at preventing and controlling hyperglycemia.

Treatment of diabetes attempts to decrease the likelihood that body tissues are harmed by hyperglycemia. The direct and indirect effects of hyperglycemia on the human vascular tree are a major source of morbidity and mortality in both type 1 and type 2 diabetes.

The injurious effects of hyperglycemia are generally separated into macrovascular complications, including coronary artery disease, peripheral arterial disease, and stroke, and microvascular complications, including diabetic nephropathy, neuropathy, and retinopathy.

Physicians need to understand the relationship between diabetes and vascular disease because diabetes prevalence continues to increase in the United States, and clinical tools for primary and secondary prevention are expanding.

Diabetic retinopathy may be the most common microvascular complication of diabetes. The risk of developing diabetic retinopathy or other microvascular complications depends on both the duration and severity of hyperglycemia.

In 2002, an estimated 877,000 lives were lost worldwide through suicide. Some developed nations had implemented national suicide prevention plans, but the effectiveness of these plans was rarely evaluated.

The review examined evidence for the effectiveness of specific suicide-preventive interventions and aimed to make recommendations for future prevention programs and research. Relevant publications were identified through MEDLINE, the Cochrane Library, and PsychINFO using search terms related to suicide prevention.

Included studies evaluated preventive interventions in major domains, including education and awareness for the general public and professionals, screening tools for at-risk individuals, treatment of psychiatric disorders, restricting access to lethal means, and responsible media reporting of suicide.

Data were extracted on primary outcomes such as completed suicide, attempted suicide, and suicidal ideation. Secondary outcomes included treatment seeking, identification of at-risk individuals, antidepressant prescription or use rates, and referrals.

Education of physicians and restricting access to lethal means were found to prevent suicide. Physician education in depression recognition and treatment and restricting access to lethal methods reduced suicide rates. The authors emphasized the need to determine which components of suicide prevention programs are effective in reducing rates of suicide and suicide attempt.

Recent studies suggest that betaKlotho and endocrine FGF19 and FGF21 redirect FGFR signaling to the regulation of metabolic homeostasis and suppression of obesity and diabetes. The study addressed which major FGFR-KLB complex mediates the differential metabolic actions of FGF19 and FGF21.

The authors determined receptor and tissue specificity of FGF21 compared with FGF19 using direct, sensitive, and quantitative binding kinetics, downstream signal transduction, and expression of early response genes after administration of FGF19 and FGF21 in mice.
FGF21 bound FGFR1 with much higher affinity than FGFR4 in the presence of KLB, whereas FGF19 bound both FGFR1 and FGFR4 in the presence of KLB with comparable affinity.

The interaction of FGF21 with FGFR4-KLB was very weak even at high concentration and could be negligible at physiological concentration. Both FGF19 and FGF21, but not FGF1, exhibited binding affinity to KLB.

FGF21 predominantly activated responses in adipose tissue and adipocytes, while FGF19 predominantly activated liver responses and to a lesser extent adipose tissue responses. The authors concluded that unlike FGF19, FGF21 was less likely to directly target the liver where FGFR4-KLB predominantly resides.

Pyruvate dehydrogenase plays a key role in regulating skeletal muscle substrate utilization. IL-6 is produced in skeletal muscle during exercise in a duration-dependent manner and has been reported to affect fatty acid oxidation, muscle glucose uptake, and PDHa activity.

The study examined whether muscle IL-6 contributes to exercise-induced PDH regulation in skeletal muscle. Skeletal muscle-specific IL-6 knockout mice and floxed littermate controls completed a single bout of treadmill exercise for 10, 60, or 120 minutes, with rested mice of each genotype serving as basal controls.

The respiratory exchange ratio was overall higher in IL-6 MKO mice than in control mice during the 120 minutes of treadmill exercise, while RER decreased during exercise independent of genotype. AMPK and ACC phosphorylation also increased with exercise independent of genotype.

PDHa activity was higher in control mice at 10 and 60 minutes of exercise than at rest but remained unchanged in IL-6 MKO mice. PDHa activity was also higher in IL-6 MKO mice than in control mice at rest and at 60 minutes of exercise.

Neither PDH phosphorylation nor acetylation could explain the genotype differences in PDHa activity. The findings suggest that skeletal muscle IL-6 contributes to regulation of PDH at rest and during prolonged exercise and normally dampens carbohydrate utilization through effects on PDH.

Angiogenesis therapy generated excitement because it may soon have a major impact on treating patients with atherosclerotic lesions obstructing arteries that supply the myocardium or legs.

Potent therapeutic interventions are rarely free of the potential for harmful effects, and angiogenesis therapy is no exception. Reasonably powered randomized double-blind clinical studies had failed to demonstrate primary end-point efficacy.

Thoughtful consideration of serious side effects that might accompany any therapeutic benefit had been largely missing from scientific communications. The lay media shifted from enthusiasm to skepticism after a report of a young man’s death caused by injection of large amounts of adenoviral vector into the hepatic artery, unrelated to angiogenesis therapy.

For the scientific community, there had been a general lack of in-depth discussion of potential dangers inherent in angiogenesis interventions. Such discussion was considered appropriate because mechanistic data could help identify specific side effects anticipated as complications of angiogenesis therapy.

The article discussed potential complications based mainly on biological activities of vascular endothelial growth factor and fibroblast growth factor. Angiogenic agents were thought to have the potential to induce neovascularization in many different tissues.
